top.description: Yankees predicted to replace Austin Wells with Cubs free agent catcher originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees are in the market for a right-handed hitting catcher. They can keep Ali Sanchez around as depth, but they should target a better hitter to platoon with Austin Wells. Overall, Wells had a disappointing 2026 season. Offensively, he hit .186/.292/.332 with 14 home runs and a .624 OPS. As their everyday backstop, the Yankees were likely hoping for much more. To help fix their lack of production from behind the plate, Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter predicted the Yankees will sign an 11-year veteran who spent the past two seasons with the Chicago Cubs . "The Yankees got a .196 average and .600 OPS from the catcher position last season, including a 74 OPS+ from incumbent starter Austin Wells. "With a .122/.192/.244 line against left-handed pitching, they at least need to find him a right-handed hitting platoon partner, and veteran Carson Kelly would be a clear upgrade," Reuter wrote. Kelly can help solve New York's problems against left-handed pitching. He hit .298 with a .375 OBP and .871 OPS in 121 at-bats versus southpaws last year. Either way, a one-to two-year deal seems to be in the cards for the 32-year-old, and the Yankees are a logical landing spot. top.title: Report card: Bills beat Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving
top.description: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs on their way to a 13-10 victory on Thanksgiving night. The Bills muddled through a chilly, rain-soaked game to win with a last-second field goal from Tyler Bass. Buffalo's aerial attack was grounded by the weather. Quarterback Josh Allen struggled through most of the game, throwing two interceptions and several inaccurate passes. While the abysmal conditions limited the passing attack, it did send the Bills back to an old-school ground-and-pound attack. James Cook rushed 32 times and scored the Bills only touchdown. The defense kept the Chiefs from gaining any sort of rhythm. Buffalo allowed only one touchdown, which was an Emmett Johnson one-yard dive on the opening drive of the second half. The Bills benefited from a Harrison Butker miss, which gave the Bills some life as the fourth quarter continued. Bass was good from 54 and 57 yards in the fourth quarter, ultimately giving Buffalo its seventh consecutive victory. Here is how Bills Wire grades the Thanksgiving performance: Passing offense: F The weather conditions were horrendous for any sort of explosive plays to be completed through the air. Even still, there was hope that Allen would be a little better than a 10-of-21 passing day. Allen totaled only 81 yards through the air. Both of Allen's interceptions were inaccurate balls that led to the turnovers. It was disappointing that Joe Brady could not figure out something to get a bit more out of the passing attack. Thank goodness for the defense and James Cook; otherwise, this game would have been a Kansas City victory. Khalil Shakir led the Bills with three catches for 33 yards. Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore, and Ty Johnson each reeled in two passes. Patrick Mahomes, playing in the same exact conditions (obviously), doubled-up Allen, throwing for 174 yards. It was possible to move the ball a bit through the air. Allen just didn't do it. Rushing offense: A- James Cook is usurping Allen's spot as Buffalo's offensive MVP. Cook was patient, setting up runs and battling for any additional yards he could obtain. He rushed 32 times, which was half of the number of the Bills offensive plays on the game. Cook totaled 117 yards, good for a 3.7-yard-per-carry average. He scurried into the end zone for Buffalo's lone touchdown on the day. Allen rushed seven times for 43 yards. As has been customary for Buffalo, the Bills succeeded on several short-yardage attempts with Allen quarterback dives. The Bills lack a rushing option beyond Cook in the backfield. Ray Davis managed six yards on four carries. Pass defense: A- Buffalo's pass defense did a solid job of limiting the Chiefs. Kansas City did make a few decent plays with Travis Kelce finding space against Buffalo's secondary. However, for the most part, the Bills won more of the battles. top.title: Shocking thrashing! Schalke 04 crushed by Paderborn in promoted sides' clash
top.description: SC Paderborn 07 v FC Schalke 04 - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Striker Edin Dzeko returned to the starting line-up, but Bundesliga newcomers Schalke 04 suffered a humiliating defeat a week before the Ruhr derby against Borussia Dortmund. Miron Muslic's alarmingly poor side lost 8-1 (3-0) away to fellow promoted side SC Paderborn, extending their winless run to eight competitive matches. Paderborn claimed their third home victory and moved into mid-table for the time being. Jano ter Horst put the hosts ahead with his first goal of the season (21). Stefano Marino scored a hat-trick (39, 45+4, 57), while Steffen Tigges (55), Deniz Zeitler (73), Gabriel Vidovic (85, penalty) and Felix Götze (90+6) also found the net. Adil Aouchiche scored Schalke's consolation goal (59). Last season, the Gelsenkirchen club had narrowly won both meetings in the second division. Muslic said Schalke wanted to approach the match "with great responsibility and unity", but they squandered a huge early chance. Junior Adamu got a shot away after a mistake by Mattes Hansen, only for goalkeeper Nahuel Noll to save (2). The 15,000 spectators in the sold-out arena saw the hosts make the more active, if nervier, start. Marino had the best chance after a counter-attack, but Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius saved (17). Schalke then had to replace Junior Dina Ebimbe, who injured his thigh during a footrace without any contact from an opponent (20). Shortly afterwards, ter Horst scored following a free-kick. Schalke offered little. Dzeko, a peripheral figure in the Bundesliga up to that point, barely made an impression either. "I can't make allowances based on names," Muslic had said before the match, but he nevertheless started the 40-year-old for the third time this season. The visitors perked up after conceding, with Hasan Kurucay's shot going narrowly wide (33). Paderborn, though, kept finding gaps in the second-division champions' usually solid defence. Marino fired well over in the 34th minute, but the East Westphalian side's top scorer doubled the lead shortly afterwards with a superb solo run, then struck again in stoppage time. Schalke came out with a little more energy after the break, but Paderborn repeatedly caught them on the counter-attack.

top.title: Undermanned Bayern held at Hamburg after Kimmich sees red
top.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich walks off after his red card against Hamburg on Saturday. (Ibrahim OT) Injury-ravaged Bayern Munich were held to a scoreless draw away at Hamburg in the Bundesliga on Saturday, with captain Joshua Kimmich sent off in the first half for a hair pull, while Schalke fell to a calamitous 8-1 loss at Paderborn. The draw, Bayern's second in two league games, leaves them a point behind league leaders Borussia Dortmund, who host Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday. Kimmich's moment of madness is the latest setback in a horror week in the Bavarian capital. In addition to their injury woes, club executives have been sharply criticised after launching a public campaign to pressure midfielder Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Bayern lost their first match of the season with a 2-1 defeat away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. Coming into the match, Bayern had won 14 of their past 16 matches with Hamburg and had not tasted defeat against them since 2009. Bayern had travelled to Hamburg with a decimated forward line, missing five attacking players including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane through injury. Bayern's lack of forward options was obvious from the opening minute, with the defending champions dominating possession but reduced to taking long-range efforts on goal. The visitors' hopes of an unlikely win took a hit just before the break, when Kimmich was shown a straight red for pulling Alexander Rossing-Lelesiit's hair. Clear goal chances were few and far between for both sides in the second half, with Bayern's appeals for a stoppage-time penalty for a foul on Luis Diaz waved away. The Bavarian giants will look to get back to winning ways when they host high-flying Hertha Berlin, who are on track for promotion after winning 12 of their 13 Bundesliga 2 games this season, in the German Cup on Tuesday. Elsewhere on Saturday, Paderborn thumped struggling Schalke 8-1 to more than double the biggest Bundesliga win in their history. Stefano Marino scored three while Jano ter Horst, Steffen Tigges, Deniz Zeitler, Gabriel Vidovic and Felix Goetze also got on the scoresheet in the romp. Schalke, who were promoted in the summer, host arch-rivals Dortmund next week. Mainz scored twice in the final five minutes to sink Union Berlin 2-1 at home, leaving the capital club in the automatic relegation places. Cologne cruised to a 5-0 home victory over promoted Elversberg, with Marius Buelter hitting a hat-trick and Germany winger Said El Mala bagging a brace. Later on Saturday, Stuttgart hope to rebound from their midweek Champions League loss at Inter Milan when they host Eintracht Frankfurt. dwi/nf

top.title: A silly red card and more injuries - Hamburg and Bayern settle for a goalless draw
top.description: A silly red card and more injuries - Hamburg and Bayern settle for a goalless draw The revived Nord-Süd-Klassiker ended without goals on Saturday, yet there was no shortage of drama at a sold-out Volksparkstadion. While Mario Vušković celebrated a clean sheet on his emotional Bundesliga debut for Hamburger SV, a youthful FC Bayern side saw Joshua Kimmich dismissed before halftime and Konrad Laimer limp off late on in a hard-fought 0-0 stalemate. Here is our full match report: Match report: HSV vs. FC Bayern The afternoon began on an emotional note for the hosts, as Mario Vušković was handed his first-ever Bundesliga start after club captain Nicolás Capaldo failed to recover in time. Alongside him, 17-year-old left-back Louis Lemke - born after HSV’s last top-flight victory over Bayern - helped anchor a backline immediately tested by the visitors. Vincent Kompany named Bayern’s youngest Bundesliga starting XI in over eight-and-a-half years, and the absence of sidelined stars Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Jamal Musiala, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Luis Díaz, who was on the bench at least, was evident in the final third. While Bayern controlled the tempo and possession and carved out more opportunities, they lacked their usual cutting edge to punish the “Rothosen”. Just as it seemed the sides would head into the dressing rooms on even terms, the match boiled over in the 44th minute. Following a shove and provocation from HSV talent Alexander Røssing-Lelesiit, Joshua Kimmich reacted by lightly pulling the HSV attacker's hair, leaving the referee with little choice but to brandish a straight red card. In immediate response to going down to ten men, Kompany turned to his bench for the start of the second half, introducing Colombian winger Luis Díaz to inject much-needed firepower. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Bayern started the second period brightly. However, the story of the first half persisted: the champions progressed into the final third with relative ease, yet consistently lacked the sharp movement, positioning, and clinical finishing required to beat Daniel Heuer Fernandes. As the clock ticked down, Hamburg grew increasingly dangerous on the break, with Fábio Vieira, Albert Grønbæk, and Martin Adeline all coming close to snatching a famous winner. Compounding Bayern’s difficult afternoon, second-half substitute Konrad Laimer was forced off with an injury in the 87th minute , raising further questions about an injury curse hovering over Kompany’s squad. Bayern briefly appealed for a late penalty just before the final whistle when Díaz went down inside the box, but the referee waved play on. For Vušković, meanwhile, walking off with a clean sheet against the German record champions marked a dream start to his Bundesliga career as the contest finished 0-0.

top.title: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr.
top.description: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr. originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays missed out on Tarik Skubal, and they missed out on Teruaki Sato this offseason. But they've already begun to pivot, landing Kaima Taira and Jazz Chisholm Jr. While those are two notable additions, the Blue Jays might not be close to being done. They offered Skubal $400 million, and the Taira and Chisholm deals aren't even close to half their offer to Skubal. So, it shouldn't be a surprise if they get involved elsewhere. Andy McCullough of The Athletic named the Blue Jays as the "ideal landing spot" for free-agent Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki. Even after landing Chisholm, the Blue Jays would be a great landing spot for Suzuki this offseason. Seiya Suzuki's 'ideal' landing spot is with Blue Jays "The Blue Jays have money to spend and a zeal to spend it," McCullough writes. "... The team needs more outfield help, and Suzuki has been a steady performer since arriving in America in 2022." Chisholm will help out the Blue Jays' infield, but this team could use help in the outfield. Jonatan Clase, Brett Bateman and Nathan Lukes could all start for the Blue Jays in the outfield next season. While there is some appeal to all three, adding an elite hitter like Suzuki, who has the ability to hit 26 home runs and also control the strike zone, would be an incredible pickup for the Blue Jays this offseason. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news Suzuki might be a little bit older, at 32 years old; he's coming off a strong 2026 season in which he had a .270 batting average with 26 homers, 5.1 bWAR, and elite defense in the outfield. With the Cubs landing Sato this offseason, it would seem Suzuki might not return to the Cubs this offseason, especially with Suzuki likely to seek a $120 million deal like what Sato got. It might be a lot of money for the Blue Jays to spend on Suzuki, but with their willingness to spend big this offseason, overpaying a little bit to guarantee they land Suzuki, arguably the best bat available this offseason, would make a lot of sense. Being able to add both Suzuki and Chisholm in one offseason would be quite the haul for the Blue Jays. Chisholm's deal wasn't too expensive, so a big Suzuki contract wouldn't hurt as bad if they land the Cubs star outfielder. top.title: Farrell says low crowd in Ireland win 'a shame'
top.description: Farrell is not convinced on the merits of kicking off finals weekend with a Friday double-header [Getty Images] Ireland head coach Andy Farrell said it was a "shame" his side's Nations Championship victory over Australia was played in front of a low crowd at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium. Friday night's fifth-place play-off attracted an attendance of just 32,000 with the uppermost tier of the 82,000-capacity stadium entirely closed. Ireland beat the Wallabies 38-14 after Italy overcame Fiji on the first day of the inaugural competition's finals day weekend at the home of England rugby. Ticket sales for Saturday and Sunday's action, which are headlined by England v New Zealand and the final between South Africa and France, have been stronger, but Farrell questioned the Friday night double-bill. "I'd love to spend some time to have a think about it, I've been preparing a team and you're busy doing that," he said. "But off the top of my head, I don't know whether the Friday night thing works or being at the same venue. If we'd have played at the Aviva (Stadium in Dublin), it would have been full. "They look like little things, but they're not, they mean a lot to the fans, like when you don't know where your team's playing and then you're trying to get a flight and all of a sudden they're £1,700. It doesn't fit." top.title: Why Marc Marquez was penalised for leaving the Valencia grid - although he did nothing wrong
top.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez’s final MotoGP sprint race on Saturday was disrupted by a problem beyond his control and by a penalty that affected his result. It was a penalty many fans disagreed with, judging by its jeering reception from the crowd at Valencia. The start of the final sprint race of the 2026 season was delayed by a problem rarely seen before: an issue with the lights. The red lights took too long to go out, prompting complaints from the entire grid, who raised their hands to signal that the start procedure was taking far too long. Read Also: Marc Marquez's Ducati catches fire in aborted Valencia GP sprint start In truth, there had already been delays in race control procedures over the weekend. As early as Q2, it was noticeable that it took far too long for a yellow flag to be displayed following a crash by Ai Ogura in the final minutes. In fact, Marco Bezzecchi had time to pass that point, eight seconds after the crash, without encountering the signal, which was displayed a further two seconds later. This is what allowed him to secure pole position without losing his best lap time, as would have been stipulated by the FIM sporting regulations were a yellow flag displayed. Read Also: MotoGP Valencia GP: Marco Bezzecchi scorches to pole position, Marc Marquez second However, the delay in the start caused even more of a mess. Today’s MotoGP bikes are prototypes not designed to be stationary, when the lack of cooling quickly causes their systems to overheat. That is exactly what happened to Marquez’s Ducati, which was in second position on the starting grid. Whilst the other bikes remained unaffected, the Italian machine began to emit a noticeable amount of smoke. Marc tried to start his bike, mainly to get some fresh air to it, but was unable to do so. The Ducati then caught fire, causing Marquez to throw himself off it in a bid to avoid being burnt. However, he still indicated that he had sustained some injuries, with parts of his leathers charred black. As a result, the bike was rendered unusable and had to be put out by the fire brigade using an extinguisher. Marquez headed straight for the pits, as did the bike he was due to start the race on, and went to collect the second one, already prepared by his team - whilst the sprint start was cancelled under a red flag due to the incident. top.description: Sebastian Vettel's damning recollection of his Ferrari days. (Source: MEGA) Four-time F1 world champion Sebastian Vettel has shared a damning verdict on his time at Ferrari. The German former racing driver stated that the team lacked the courage to make major changes and hence found itself being beaten by the likes of Mercedes regularly during his time at the team. “I think what I learned during my time is that perhaps Ferrari lacked a bit of courage to change in that respect,” Vettel told Nextgen-Auto . “We're too tense, we're not relaxed, we're not having as much fun. The camaraderie isn't there, the trust isn't there,” he also recalled telling the team. Sebastian Vettel joined Ferrari in 2015. But much like many drivers before and after him, he national found it incredibly difficult to change the culture at Maranello and bring the team back to winning ways. In his six seasons at Ferrari, Vettel won 14 races but failed to win a drivers’ title or take Ferrari back to the top of the constructors’ standings. His best results came in 2017 and 2018, as he finished runner-up to Lewis Hamilton on both occasions, with an early-season title challenge coming crashing down in the latter half of both years. He explained that the Scuderia ran too hot at the beginning of the year but failed to maintain that level of intensity throughout the season due to burnout. “We were all exhausted. nigeria.title: 2027 : Atiku, Obi relying on regional support to win election, Shettima says
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi of relying on regional support in their bid to win the 2027 presidential election. Shettima made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he questioned the opposition candidates’ campaign strategies and their efforts to build support across the country. He said Obi had visited 17 states, including all five states in the South-East and all South-South states except Rivers, but had made limited visits to other regions. According to Shettima, Obi had visited only Kaduna State in the North and Lagos State in the South-West. He also accused the Labour Party’s 2023 presidential candidate of attempting to use religious divisions to advance his political ambition, insisting that elections could not be won through division. “You cannot win election through divisions. We win elections through negotiation, through compromises, through bridge building,” the Vice-President said. Shettima also criticised Atiku’s campaign activities, claiming that the former vice-president had visited only six states and had not travelled to any state in Southern Nigeria. “My brother Atiku Abubakar, he has so far visited six states in the Federation. He has not visited one state in Southern Nigeria. He has concentrated purely in the North,” he said. The Vice-President argued that presidential candidates needed support beyond their traditional political strongholds to secure victory, citing former President Muhammadu Buhari’s eventual success after building an alliance with the South-West. He said Buhari’s support in the North alone had not been enough to secure the presidency until he formed an alliance with the South-West. Shettima expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu would defeat the opposition candidates in the 2027 election. The exercise witnessed a predominantly female turnout, with relatively few male voters seen at several polling units visited. At Aliero Housing Estate 006 Primary School polling unit, female voters turned out for accreditation, while only a few male voters were sighted. Security personnel, including officers of the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and State Security Service (SCIB), were deployed to provide security during the exercise. INEC ad hoc staff at the polling unit confirmed that the BVAS machines were functioning effectively during voter authentication. A visit to Gwadangaji 001 polling unit also showed a low turnout, with a few female voters presenting themselves for accreditation and no male voters sighted at the time. The voters were seen checking their names on the lists displayed on the walls before proceeding with the exercise. However, at Justice Ibrahim Umar polling unit in the GRA NEPA area, a relatively large number of female voters turned out for the mock exercise. The ad hoc staff confirmed that the two BVAS machines provided for the polling unit were working effectively, adding that no malfunction had been recorded since the exercise commenced at 9 a.m. Meanwhile, an APC stakeholder, Alhaji Abubakar ABK, described the exercise as impressive and peaceful. He attributed the participation of female voters to what he described as the humanitarian interventions of Governor Idris, expressing optimism that voters would turn out in large numbers during the January 2027 general elections. nigeria.title: 2027: Nigerians determined to vote out APC, says Hashim
nigeria.description: Presidential candidate of the Accord Party, Dr. Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has declared that Nigerians have made up their minds to vote against the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election, accusing the President Bola Tinubu-led administration of worsening the country’s economic and security challenges. Hashim made the declaration on Saturday in Abuja during the flag-off of his presidential campaign, where he promised to build a $4 trillion economy within eight years if elected president. He said economic hardship, rising insecurity, widespread poverty and what he described as the significant collapse of the economy under the APC-led government had strengthened Nigerians’ determination to change the country’s leadership. The Accord presidential candidate cited the reported reach of his recent interview on Symfoni Podcast, which he said was watched by almost 10 million Nigerians and attracted over one million positive reactions, as evidence of growing interest in his presidential ambition. He also alleged that some APC leaders were complicit in the worsening security situation, saying banditry and other forms of criminality had devastated communities across several states. According to him, the 2027 general election would be different, insisting that political victory would not be determined by the ability of parties to fill stadiums during campaigns. He accused the ruling party of already campaigning against itself through its handling of the country’s affairs. “Nigerians will cook APC with cold water,” Hashim declared in Hausa, drawing a loud ovation from the crowd. He further accused the APC of attempting to manipulate the 2027 elections and criticised what he described as exorbitant charges for political campaign billboards in Abuja. nigeria.description: The City Boy Movement has hailed the rise in Nigeria’s gross foreign reserves to $54.13 billion, describing the development as evidence of progress under President Bola Tinubu’s economic reform agenda. The group said the reserves had reached their second-highest level on record since 1999, surpassed only by the $62.08 billion peak recorded in September 2008, when the global financial crisis was unfolding. In a statement titled, “Why Tinubu 4+4? Foreign Reserves Edition,” the movement said Nigeria’s foreign reserves had increased significantly under the Tinubu administration, rising from $32.29 billion in May 2023 to $54.13 billion in November 2026. It put the increase at $21.84 billion, representing nearly 68 per cent growth since the President assumed office. According to the group, the latest figures place Nigeria’s foreign reserves above the peak levels recorded in several years, including 2009, 2007, 2013, 2018, 2025, 2019, 2012 and 2014. The movement noted that Nigeria’s reserves peaked at $53.25 billion in 2009, $51.33 billion in 2007, $48.86 billion in 2013 and $47.87 billion in 2018. It added that the $54.13 billion recorded in 2026 represented the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. While acknowledging the difficulties associated with the economic reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration, the group argued that the latest reserve figures indicated that the policies were beginning to yield positive results. It said the growth in foreign reserves was an important development in assessing the direction of the economy, expressing optimism that the country was moving towards greater economic prosperity. “The significance is in the history. Even though the reforms have been difficult, the numbers are beginning to tell their own story. We are on the way to prosperity,” the statement said. The movement also expressed appreciation to Tinubu for what it described as progress in the management of the country’s external reserves, reaffirming its support for the President. The figures cited by the group were attributed to data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN). However, the movement’s assessment comes amid continuing public debate over the impact of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly their effects on inflation, living costs, businesses and household welfare. While higher foreign reserves can strengthen a country’s capacity to meet external obligations and support confidence in its economy, the extent to which the increase translates into improved living conditions remains a key measure of the overall success of the reforms. At Ibeku High School, one of the designated polling centres, Vanguard observed at about noon that no voter had turned up, while INEC officials waited for participants. nigeria.title: Dangote Refinery set to list on NGX December 1
nigeria.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals FZE is scheduled to list 125,458,915,901 ordinary shares at N525 per share on the Main Board of Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday, 1 December 2026. The listing is expected to add approximately N65.87 trillion to the market capitalisation of NGX. The listing follows the company’s Initial Public Offering (IPO), which attracted approximately 3.8 million subscribers from 121 countries, including all 54 African countries, reflecting unprecedented investor participation in a Nigerian public equity offering. With a minimum subscription of N5,250 for 10 ordinary shares, the offer enabled investors across income groups and geographical locations to participate in the ownership of one of Africa’s largest industrial enterprises. Speaking at the launch of the IPO in September, Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, described the offer as an opportunity to broaden public ownership and enable more Nigerians and Africans to participate in industrial wealth creation. “The Dangote refinery IPO is more than an investment opportunity; it is an opportunity for millions of Nigerians and Africans to build lasting wealth through ownership of a world-class industrial asset,” Dangote said. Investor participation at this scale was facilitated by NGX Invest, the SEC-approved digital capital-raising platform launched by Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) in June 2024. By enabling a network of 186 distribution channels, including stockbrokers, banks, fintech platforms and WhatsApp, NGX Invest provided the rail that significantly broadened access to the public offer. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “The listing of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will mark an important milestone for Nigeria’s capital market, demonstrating its capacity to support large-scale industrial enterprises and mobilise long-term capital. The breadth of investor participation in the public offer also reflects the progress we have made in expanding market access. Through technology, strategic partnerships and a diverse distribution network, we are connecting more people to investment opportunities and more businesses to capital.” According to the company’s prospectus, net proceeds from the IPO will partly finance an estimated US$14.3 billion expansion programme designed to double refining capacity from 700,000 to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day. The transaction underscores the capital market’s strategic role in financing industrial expansion, broadening economic participation and supporting Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a US$1 trillion economy. business.title: Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps. Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. business.title: Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.title: New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). sports.title: Report card: Bills beat Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving
sports.description: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs on their way to a 13-10 victory on Thanksgiving night. The Bills muddled through a chilly, rain-soaked game to win with a last-second field goal from Tyler Bass. Buffalo's aerial attack was grounded by the weather. Quarterback Josh Allen struggled through most of the game, throwing two interceptions and several inaccurate passes. While the abysmal conditions limited the passing attack, it did send the Bills back to an old-school ground-and-pound attack. James Cook rushed 32 times and scored the Bills only touchdown. The defense kept the Chiefs from gaining any sort of rhythm. Buffalo allowed only one touchdown, which was an Emmett Johnson one-yard dive on the opening drive of the second half. The Bills benefited from a Harrison Butker miss, which gave the Bills some life as the fourth quarter continued. Bass was good from 54 and 57 yards in the fourth quarter, ultimately giving Buffalo its seventh consecutive victory. Here is how Bills Wire grades the Thanksgiving performance: Passing offense: F The weather conditions were horrendous for any sort of explosive plays to be completed through the air. Even still, there was hope that Allen would be a little better than a 10-of-21 passing day. Allen totaled only 81 yards through the air. Both of Allen's interceptions were inaccurate balls that led to the turnovers. It was disappointing that Joe Brady could not figure out something to get a bit more out of the passing attack. Thank goodness for the defense and James Cook; otherwise, this game would have been a Kansas City victory. Khalil Shakir led the Bills with three catches for 33 yards. Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore, and Ty Johnson each reeled in two passes. Patrick Mahomes, playing in the same exact conditions (obviously), doubled-up Allen, throwing for 174 yards. Cook totaled 117 yards, good for a 3.7-yard-per-carry average. He scurried into the end zone for Buffalo's lone touchdown on the day. Allen rushed seven times for 43 yards. sports.title: Shocking thrashing! Schalke 04 crushed by Paderborn in promoted sides' clash
sports.description: SC Paderborn 07 v FC Schalke 04 - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Striker Edin Dzeko returned to the starting line-up, but Bundesliga newcomers Schalke 04 suffered a humiliating defeat a week before the Ruhr derby against Borussia Dortmund. Miron Muslic's alarmingly poor side lost 8-1 (3-0) away to fellow promoted side SC Paderborn, extending their winless run to eight competitive matches. Paderborn claimed their third home victory and moved into mid-table for the time being. Jano ter Horst put the hosts ahead with his first goal of the season (21). Stefano Marino scored a hat-trick (39, 45+4, 57), while Steffen Tigges (55), Deniz Zeitler (73), Gabriel Vidovic (85, penalty) and Felix Götze (90+6) also found the net. Adil Aouchiche scored Schalke's consolation goal (59). Last season, the Gelsenkirchen club had narrowly won both meetings in the second division. Muslic said Schalke wanted to approach the match "with great responsibility and unity", but they squandered a huge early chance. Junior Adamu got a shot away after a mistake by Mattes Hansen, only for goalkeeper Nahuel Noll to save (2). The 15,000 spectators in the sold-out arena saw the hosts make the more active, if nervier, start. Marino had the best chance after a counter-attack, but Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius saved (17). Schalke then had to replace Junior Dina Ebimbe, who injured his thigh during a footrace without any contact from an opponent (20). Shortly afterwards, ter Horst scored following a free-kick. Schalke offered little. Dzeko, a peripheral figure in the Bundesliga up to that point, barely made an impression either. "I can't make allowances based on names," Muslic had said before the match, but he nevertheless started the 40-year-old for the third time this season. The visitors perked up after conceding, with Hasan Kurucay's shot going narrowly wide (33). Paderborn, though, kept finding gaps in the second-division champions' usually solid defence. Marino fired well over in the 34th minute, but the East Westphalian side's top scorer doubled the lead shortly afterwards with a superb solo run, then struck again in stoppage time. Schalke came out with a little more energy after the break, but Paderborn repeatedly caught them on the counter-attack.

sports.title: Undermanned Bayern held at Hamburg after Kimmich sees red
sports.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich walks off after his red card against Hamburg on Saturday. (Ibrahim OT) Injury-ravaged Bayern Munich were held to a scoreless draw away at Hamburg in the Bundesliga on Saturday, with captain Joshua Kimmich sent off in the first half for a hair pull, while Schalke fell to a calamitous 8-1 loss at Paderborn. The draw, Bayern's second in two league games, leaves them a point behind league leaders Borussia Dortmund, who host Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday. Kimmich's moment of madness is the latest setback in a horror week in the Bavarian capital. In addition to their injury woes, club executives have been sharply criticised after launching a public campaign to pressure midfielder Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Bayern lost their first match of the season with a 2-1 defeat away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. Coming into the match, Bayern had won 14 of their past 16 matches with Hamburg and had not tasted defeat against them since 2009. Bayern had travelled to Hamburg with a decimated forward line, missing five attacking players including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane through injury. Bayern's lack of forward options was obvious from the opening minute, with the defending champions dominating possession but reduced to taking long-range efforts on goal. The visitors' hopes of an unlikely win took a hit just before the break, when Kimmich was shown a straight red for pulling Alexander Rossing-Lelesiit's hair. Clear goal chances were few and far between for both sides in the second half, with Bayern's appeals for a stoppage-time penalty for a foul on Luis Diaz waved away. The Bavarian giants will look to get back to winning ways when they host high-flying Hertha Berlin, who are on track for promotion after winning 12 of their 13 Bundesliga 2 games this season, in the German Cup on Tuesday. Elsewhere on Saturday, Paderborn thumped struggling Schalke 8-1 to more than double the biggest Bundesliga win in their history. Stefano Marino scored three while Jano ter Horst, Steffen Tigges, Deniz Zeitler, Gabriel Vidovic and Felix Goetze also got on the scoresheet in the romp. Schalke, who were promoted in the summer, host arch-rivals Dortmund next week. Mainz scored twice in the final five minutes to sink Union Berlin 2-1 at home, leaving the capital club in the automatic relegation places. Cologne cruised to a 5-0 home victory over promoted Elversberg, with Marius Buelter hitting a hat-trick and Germany winger Said El Mala bagging a brace. Later on Saturday, Stuttgart hope to rebound from their midweek Champions League loss at Inter Milan when they host Eintracht Frankfurt. dwi/nf

sports.title: A silly red card and more injuries - Hamburg and Bayern settle for a goalless draw
sports.description: A silly red card and more injuries - Hamburg and Bayern settle for a goalless draw The revived Nord-Süd-Klassiker ended without goals on Saturday, yet there was no shortage of drama at a sold-out Volksparkstadion. While Mario Vušković celebrated a clean sheet on his emotional Bundesliga debut for Hamburger SV, a youthful FC Bayern side saw Joshua Kimmich dismissed before halftime and Konrad Laimer limp off late on in a hard-fought 0-0 stalemate. Here is our full match report: Match report: HSV vs. FC Bayern The afternoon began on an emotional note for the hosts, as Mario Vušković was handed his first-ever Bundesliga start after club captain Nicolás Capaldo failed to recover in time. Alongside him, 17-year-old left-back Louis Lemke - born after HSV’s last top-flight victory over Bayern - helped anchor a backline immediately tested by the visitors. Vincent Kompany named Bayern’s youngest Bundesliga starting XI in over eight-and-a-half years, and the absence of sidelined stars Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Jamal Musiala, Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Luis Díaz, who was on the bench at least, was evident in the final third. While Bayern controlled the tempo and possession and carved out more opportunities, they lacked their usual cutting edge to punish the “Rothosen”. Just as it seemed the sides would head into the dressing rooms on even terms, the match boiled over in the 44th minute. Following a shove and provocation from HSV talent Alexander Røssing-Lelesiit, Joshua Kimmich reacted by lightly pulling the HSV attacker's hair, leaving the referee with little choice but to brandish a straight red card. In immediate response to going down to ten men, Kompany turned to his bench for the start of the second half, introducing Colombian winger Luis Díaz to inject much-needed firepower. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Bayern started the second period brightly. However, the story of the first half persisted: the champions progressed into the final third with relative ease, yet consistently lacked the sharp movement, positioning, and clinical finishing required to beat Daniel Heuer Fernandes. As the clock ticked down, Hamburg grew increasingly dangerous on the break, with Fábio Vieira, Albert Grønbæk, and Martin Adeline all coming close to snatching a famous winner. Compounding Bayern’s difficult afternoon, second-half substitute Konrad Laimer was forced off with an injury in the 87th minute , raising further questions about an injury curse hovering over Kompany’s squad. Bayern briefly appealed for a late penalty just before the final whistle when Díaz went down inside the box, but the referee waved play on. For Vušković, meanwhile, walking off with a clean sheet against the German record champions marked a dream start to his Bundesliga career as the contest finished 0-0.

sports.title: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr.
sports.description: Blue Jays are 'ideal landing spot' for Cubs 26-HR free agent despite Jazz Chisholm Jr. originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Blue Jays missed out on Tarik Skubal, and they missed out on Teruaki Sato this offseason. But they've already begun to pivot, landing Kaima Taira and Jazz Chisholm Jr. While those are two notable additions, the Blue Jays might not be close to being done. They offered Skubal $400 million, and the Taira and Chisholm deals aren't even close to half their offer to Skubal. So, it shouldn't be a surprise if they get involved elsewhere. Andy McCullough of The Athletic named the Blue Jays as the "ideal landing spot" for free-agent Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki. Even after landing Chisholm, the Blue Jays would be a great landing spot for Suzuki this offseason. Seiya Suzuki's 'ideal' landing spot is with Blue Jays "The Blue Jays have money to spend and a zeal to spend it," McCullough writes. "... The team needs more outfield help, and Suzuki has been a steady performer since arriving in America in 2022." Chisholm will help out the Blue Jays' infield, but this team could use help in the outfield. Jonatan Clase, Brett Bateman and Nathan Lukes could all start for the Blue Jays in the outfield next season. While there is some appeal to all three, adding an elite hitter like Suzuki, who has the ability to hit 26 home runs and also control the strike zone, would be an incredible pickup for the Blue Jays this offseason. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news Suzuki might be a little bit older, at 32 years old; he's coming off a strong 2026 season in which he had a .270 batting average with 26 homers, 5.1 bWAR, and elite defense in the outfield. With the Cubs landing Sato this offseason, it would seem Suzuki might not return to the Cubs this offseason, especially with Suzuki likely to seek a $120 million deal like what Sato got. It might be a lot of money for the Blue Jays to spend on Suzuki, but with their willingness to spend big this offseason, overpaying a little bit to guarantee they land Suzuki, arguably the best bat available this offseason, would make a lot of sense. Being able to add both Suzuki and Chisholm in one offseason would be quite the haul for the Blue Jays. Chisholm's deal wasn't too expensive, so a big Suzuki contract wouldn't hurt as bad if they land the Cubs star outfielder. Friday night's fifth-place play-off attracted an attendance of just 32,000 with the uppermost tier of the 82,000-capacity stadium entirely closed. Ireland beat the Wallabies 38-14 after Italy overcame Fiji on the first day of the inaugural competition's finals day weekend at the home of England rugby. Ticket sales for Saturday and Sunday's action, which are headlined by England v New Zealand and the final between South Africa and France, have been stronger, but Farrell questioned the Friday night double-bill. "I'd love to spend some time to have a think about it, I've been preparing a team and you're busy doing that," he said. "But off the top of my head, I don't know whether the Friday night thing works or being at the same venue. If we'd have played at the Aviva (Stadium in Dublin), it would have been full. "They look like little things, but they're not, they mean a lot to the fans, like when you don't know where your team's playing and then you're trying to get a flight and all of a sudden they're £1,700. It doesn't fit." Farrell senses 'shift' as Ireland finish 2026 strongly Ulster resurgence aids Ireland's perfect November Format 'doesn't make sense' Farrell said he enjoyed parts of the spectacle, which included a pre-game performance from British popstar Myles Smith. "I love what they're trying to do. I love the razzmatazz and coming into the ground it felt different. It felt like it was trying to be like an event, like a concert," he added. "It was just a shame that we couldn't get the people through the door. The pre-match hype looked fantastic on the TV – from what I saw in the dressing room anyway. "The 16:40 game – I felt for those boys really. And Sam Prendergast didn't get anything for man of the match, so playing for fifth place obviously didn't mean much." Ireland won five of their six pool games to finish third in the northern hemisphere table behind France and England, while Australia finished third in the southern hemisphere standings behind South Africa and New Zealand after losing four matches. sports.title: Why Marc Marquez was penalised for leaving the Valencia grid - although he did nothing wrong
sports.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez’s final MotoGP sprint race on Saturday was disrupted by a problem beyond his control and by a penalty that affected his result. It was a penalty many fans disagreed with, judging by its jeering reception from the crowd at Valencia. The start of the final sprint race of the 2026 season was delayed by a problem rarely seen before: an issue with the lights. The red lights took too long to go out, prompting complaints from the entire grid, who raised their hands to signal that the start procedure was taking far too long. Read Also: Marc Marquez's Ducati catches fire in aborted Valencia GP sprint start In truth, there had already been delays in race control procedures over the weekend. As early as Q2, it was noticeable that it took far too long for a yellow flag to be displayed following a crash by Ai Ogura in the final minutes. In fact, Marco Bezzecchi had time to pass that point, eight seconds after the crash, without encountering the signal, which was displayed a further two seconds later. This is what allowed him to secure pole position without losing his best lap time, as would have been stipulated by the FIM sporting regulations were a yellow flag displayed. sports.title: F1's latest feud heats up following another tense on-track encounter
sports.description: Carlos Sainz has once again taken issue with Franco Colapinto 's on-track behaviour following an incident during FP2 at the Qatar Grand Prix, just a week after a similar encounter in Las Vegas. While the feuds between Max Verstappen and George Russell and between the two Ferrari drivers have been among the most heated in recent weeks, tensions have also been growing between Sainz and Colapinto. The pair had already been involved in a tense moment down the Strip in Las Vegas, when the Argentine attempted an aggressive move during free practice, coming dangerously close to making contact with the Williams driver. During FP2 yesterday, Colapinto picked up Sainz's slipstream down the main straight before attacking the Spaniard down the inside at Turn 1. The Argentine ran wide under braking, forcing his rival to move aside to avoid contact. The incident also caught the attention of an amused George Russell, who laughed over the team radio. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Speaking to the media on Friday in Qatar, Sainz questioned the Alpine driver's approach to practice sessions, suggesting that such aggression was unnecessary given that there was nothing at stake: “It’s been a couple of Fridays that Franco has been a bit difficult with me, and I don’t understand what he’s doing on Fridays.” He then added: “He races like it’s Sunday, but I guess he’s just young.” When asked whether he would speak to Colapinto about his behaviour, the Spaniard replied: “Maybe I’ll say something.” Colapinto has been involved in more contentious incidents with other drivers this season. One such example came in Baku, where the Argentine triggered a three-car collision at Turn 1 following a Safety Car restart, taking himself, Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris out of the race. Norris, usually rather composed when speaking to the media, lost his patience on that occasion, going as far as to say: “Just some drivers that shouldn’t be in F1 , to be honest.” A few days later, having had time to cool down, Norris publicly apologised to the Alpine driver in a social media post, revealing that the pair had already spoken privately and cleared the air. Even Colapinto's own boss, Flavio Briatore, made no attempt to defend the Argentine on that occasion, describing the incident as a “very poor move for a driver of his experience” and publicly apologising to Norris and McLaren.

technology.title: Quantum: 'Five years, that's all we got…'
technology.description: SC26 in Chicago had the usual quantum booths, discussions, and hallway optimism. A lot of people were talking about integration with classical HPC and Slurm scheduling for quantum processors, co-design platforms, and GPU-accelerated error correction tools. That part is real and useful. What was harder to find was any result that changed the basic math on when quantum systems will actually do something a supercomputer can't already handle better. I had a long conversation in St. Louis (SC25) with a contact who works deep in quantum and has spent decades in HPC. He's not a skeptic for sport, although that can be fun, sure. Over a grifted free dinner in Chicago (the best kind), his take this year remains the same: the hype keeps outrunning the error rates. Quantum computers generate too many errors to give usable answers on anything interesting. Fixing that is the whole game. And that's a five-year game, minimum. Much like the Bowie anthem in the title. Qubits by the numbers There are two kinds of qubits. Physical qubits are the actual hardware: ions, superconducting circuits, and atoms in a trap. Logical qubits are the ones that do the computation. Each logical qubit is built out of many physical ones so the system can detect and correct errors while it runs. With the traditional surface-code approach, one logical qubit often needs somewhere between 500 and 2,000 physical qubits backing it up, depending on the hardware and the code. One logical qubit by itself is useless. Estimates for basic scientific modeling and small-scale simulation sit in the 100-to-500 logical-qubit range. Take the midpoint of 300. At the low end of the overhead that is 150,000 physical qubits. At the high end it is several million. That is only for early science. Commercial work like molecular mapping for pharma, large optimization problems, complex financial models, pushes into the thousands of logical qubits. National-security and encryption-related work sits even higher. Those numbers have not magically shrunk. A system that can map a modestly sized drug molecule, or run a materials simulation that is still too slow on classical machines, is the kind of workload people actually mean when they talk about useful quantum advantage. Until the logical-qubit counts get there with error rates low enough to finish the job, those problems stay on the machines we already know how to build. Ok, so let's just scale it up This is the world of HPC, we know how to scale stuff, right? Yes, but this isn't a matter of adding a few more racks. Scaling to an additional few hundred thousand physical qubits is not a rack or two or ten. It's probably a dedicated building with its own cryogenics, control electronics, and power draw that is still measured in megawatts even before you get useful logical capacity. technology.title: Unkernel and Trynix just transported computing to 2035
technology.description: What's the difference between just-for-fun demo hacks, and serious carefully designed large-scale software architecture? It's the quick-and-dirty jobs that end up transforming computing. A blog post earlier this week called 2035 came early led the Reg FOSS desk down what we thought was a fascinating, and possibly quite scary, rabbit-hole… but it turned out to be an entire warren. We thought we were still in 2026, but in turns out that in some ways, tech just leaped forward a decade. To try to convey the point of this blog post – why what had been just a fun clever little hack has the potential to take half a century of OS and hypervisor design and throw it out of the nearest window – will take quite a lot of unpacking. If you bear with us, we will try to walk you through it. To get started, we need to go back a decade or more. Stick with this: there are laughs, as well as hammers taken to beloved ideas. The year of 2035 and the ideas around that come from a remarkable talk by Gary Bernhardt of Destroy All Software, which is both funny and highly educational. It will really massively assist understanding what this article and the technology is all about if you have the time to watch the talks. The Reg FOSS desk is not at all fond of spoken-word video as a medium – we much prefer to read than listen – but the three talks we're going to mention are golden, among the very best presentations this century in all of computing and IT. Seriously, they are worth your time. As a preface, before we go into Bernhardt's half-hour information-dense talk, let's warm up with a four-minute funny one. But first, let's look at the context for that. Step 0: JavaScript is the language of web programming In 2009, Jeff Atwood laid this out in an article called All Programming is Web Programming . It's still coming true today. Software is getting very blurred around the edges. The entire SaaS industry means that massive organizations run on web apps. Tech like Electron embeds a web browser inside JavaScript apps built in Node.js, while Progressive Web Apps make websites look like local program windows. The most popular desktop Linux in the world is ChromeOS Flex, which doesn't support local native applications at all. Everything is browser windows, even the desktop. It's all built in JavaScript. And yet… Step 1: JavaScript is kind of weird and kind of bad. Bernhardt made this case in 2012, with a celebrated lightning talk called Wat , from the CodeMash conference in 2012. Wat walks through a whole list of examples of how JavaScript is a very strange programming language and does very strange things that are not at all what you might expect. Some of the jokes will make more sense to programmers, but we reckon anyone who has ever fought with a recalcitrant bit of software will get some laughs from it – and that probably applies to all readers of The Register. science.title: How moon dust and recycled cardboard could help NASA build its lunar base
science.description:
Julian Dossett is a freelance writer living in Santa Fe, New Mexico. He primarily covers the rocket industry and space exploration and, in addition to science writing, contributes travel stories to New Mexico Magazine. In 2022 and 2024, his travel writing earned IRMA Awards. Previously, he worked as a staff writer at CNET. He graduated from Texas State University in San Marcos in 2011 with a B.A. in philosophy. He owns a large collection of sci-fi pulp magazines from the 1960s.

The high cost of building on the moon has led to wide-ranging research on how to make use of the moon's most plentiful resource: the dusty regolith that covers its surface. Right now, lunar shipping runs about $544,000 per pound ($1.2 million per kilogram), so anything that astronauts can make on the moon using existing materials could help a lot. Scientists have already proposed using regolith for building 3D-printed bricks , solar arrays , and even as soil to grow potatoes . Now, a team of researchers from Purdue University in Indiana have developed an aerogel made from simulated regolith for insulating lunar habitats. New aerogels created by Purdue University researchers, made of cellulose and lunar regolith simulant, could pave the way for insulating materials made on the moon. (Image credit: Purdue University photo/John Underwood) "Sustaining a long-term presence on the moon will require us to rethink how we use local resources," Wei, professor in Purdue's James Tarpo Jr. and Margaret Tarpo Department of Chemistry, said in a Nov. 19 statement . NASA has said that it wants a long-term, sustainable moon base up and running by 2032, a goal it aims to achieve via its Artemis program . "Rather than relying on Earth to supply everything we need, we're exploring how materials already available on the moon, including waste generated by its inhabitants, could be upcycled into something essential for safe and livable habitats," Wei said. The aerogel that the Purdue researchers have been working on is a mix of fiber from cardboard waste, called cellulose, and a material that simulates regolith. They said that it could protect the people living in habitats from the moon's drastic temperature swings. "Imagine an aerogel as a high-tech thermos for a lunar base," Jacob Staker, a graduate researcher working on the study, said in the same statement. "Most of it consists of empty space that insulates the interior, helping it maintain the temperature of what's inside." The idea here is not to create the best aerogel possible, Wei said, but that "we're looking for the sweet spot where we can get the properties we need with the limited resources we have available" on the moon. The research was published in September in the journal ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.
